pages.title: Architecture and ownership boundaries
pages.purpose: Repository-wide orientation: what celld is, the three-crate ownership split, the execution-domain discipline, and a subsystem map with links.
instructions: Cover the workspace manifest rationale (workspace.dependencies centralization, release/lab profiles) and the three crates' roles.

Map the subsystem inventory (routing, gate, output gate, replication, node log, runtime, pool, deploy, fleet, telemetry) to their owning modules with a one-line responsibility each; this page is the hub, not the deep dive.
Mention docs/ as the operator-facing contract and examples/ as runnable fixtures; note that docs/testing.md describes infrastructure (TLA+, sim harness) that is not in this snapshot.
Trace the canonical control flow: HTTP ingress -> actor -> on_event -> Effect -> adapter -> versioned Event completion.

pages.title: Actor and execution boundary (celld shell)
pages.purpose: Explain the celld shell: the serial actor, effect adapters, the execution-domain boundary enforced by asyncrt plus clippy, and determinism discipline.
instructions: Cover startup.rs listener reservation policy and host_services.rs injection of process services.
Cover the asyncrt facade and the custom select macros and why the clippy disallowed list exists (spawn, clocks, fs, rand must go through the execution domain).
Do not re-explain the pure policy modules; link to the decision-core page.
Document the serial actor loop: mailbox, versioned timers (TimerSlot semantics, why deadline slots are keyed per operation), effect dispatch to adapters, and completion events.

Explain the cfg(celld_internal_tests) gating and test = false manifests: internal unit tests exist in source but the default cargo test harness does not compile them; verify how the Dockerfile test stage runs.

pages.title: Sans-I/O decision core (celld-logic)
pages.purpose: Explain the celld-logic crate: the sans-IO pure decision core, its Event/Effect vocabulary, and where each behavioral policy lives.
instructions: Document on_event as the only state-advance path, Event/Effect/State/Config vocabulary in types.rs, and the adapter contract (adapters never mutate State; they return versioned completion events).
Explain why the core exists: deterministic simulation and the docs/testing.md claims; note the actual simulator is not in this snapshot.
Note log_tier.rs is marked design-stage / not yet wired into the engine; state that boundary explicitly.

Summarize what each pure policy module decides: gate, output_gate, schedule, isolate, restore, routing, peer, pressure, wake, alarm, cron, drain, kv, queue, log_tier/log_evict, cache, sweep, sqlite, dead_node_reconciliation, http, cell.

pages.title: Cell lifecycle and placement
pages.purpose: How a cell lives on a node: activation, routing to the owner, residency states, idle eviction, hibernation, restore selection, alarms and wake.
instructions: Cover alarms and cross-node wake: wake/<date>/<cell> bucket mirror, per-node boot scan, advisory fleet waker, alarm retry backoff policy in logic/alarm.rs.
Cover cold activation: routing decides acquire/restore, logic/restore RestoreSpec fields (fresh, took_over, resume_local, prior) and the adapter's obligation not to rediscover sources.
Cover isolate pooling: one isolate per cell, v8::Locker thread independence, activation limits (CELLD_ACTIVATIONS), resident-cell caps, and the per-cell input gate allowing concurrent fetches.
Document the state machine: resident/active/idle/hibernated/inactive, constructor rerun on activation, hibernated cells keeping WebSocket clients.
Ground state names and behavior in crates/logic and the runtime/pool adapters; cite the docs/README.md lifecycle section as contract.

pages.title: Durability, fencing, and leases
pages.purpose: The two safety promises and their mechanisms: bucket CAS ownership, epoch fences, output gate RPO=0 proof, fleet node-log ensemble, takeover recovery, lease-based self-fencing.
instructions: Cover full-prefix restore rule and why the seal object was removed; distinguish code-established facts from guarantees.md narrative.
Cover self-fencing: node lease renewal cadence (CELLD_TTL_MS), lease-expiry fencing, SELF-FENCE exit code 3, terminality of the fenced state.
Cover storage prerequisites: conditional create/overwrite + read-after-write, qualified providers, probe/ storage test, CELLD_STORAGE_PROBE.
Cover the node log: per-session node-log records, takeover recovery gate (seal prior session, upload retained segments/bundles), bundle drain, hedges and gray-follower eviction config knobs.

Cover the output gate rule: no acknowledgement before a durability proof; bucket proof re-reads ownership record; fleet proof via node-log ensemble with fsynced followers, up to two followers, CELLD_DURABILITY modes.
Document the ownership record CAS protocol (create vs compare-and-swap), fencing epochs per activation, and the epoch-in-prefix data fence cells/<scope>/ltx/e<epoch>/.

pages.title: Deployment pipeline and generations
pages.purpose: How an application gets onto a fleet: celld deploy, the bucket-resident deployment objects, feature gating, generation adoption and reload, and rollout rules.
instructions: Cover the dev-mode stack (dev.rs, local_store.rs) reusing deployment/ownership/LTX with a local object store.
Document celld deploy: esbuild bundling, accepted Wrangler config subset, error on unknown keys, writing deployment objects and pointers to the bucket.

Document control_plane.rs managed sessions (celld.dev presence/explorer/module sync) as an alpha path, including CELLD_CLOUD_RESTART_ON_DEPLOY escape hatch; note upgrade-specific invariants (v0.1->v0.2 stop-all, v0.2.x->v0.3 rolling, v0.3->v0.4 stop-all) only where the repo records them.

Document generation adoption at runtime: 30s pointer poll, build-beside-then-switch, request draining to old generation, safe-point object migration, forced move after CELLD_DEPLOY_MAX_AGE_S, /reload and /state visibility.
Document node discovery via nodes/ leases and fleet/peer-auth.json HMAC bootstrap by the first node.
Document protocol.rs as the durable bucket contract: Manifest, DeployPointer, module refs, asset index, feature-gate strings, queue consumer attachment, deployment_version.

pages.title: Change guide and verification
pages.purpose: How to safely change this repository: what verification exists locally, where behavior belongs, and step-by-step recipes for representative maintenance tasks.
instructions: Document the verification reality in this snapshot: cfg(celld_internal_tests) gated in-source tests, test = false manifests, the Dockerfile test stage (cargo test + clippy -D warnings, sqlite3 CLI for the ltx fault oracle), and clippy.toml disallowed-methods as a compile-visible architecture guard.

Give change recipes grounded in code: adding a CELLD_* env var (env_vars helpers + startup report + docs/README table), adding a Workers API surface (js binding + logic policy + examples/ + cloudflare-compat.md), changing a bucket-resident object type (protocol.rs + readers on old nodes + upgrade rule), adding a durable type or reserved class, moving logic into the core (pure policy in celld-logic + adapter effect + versioned event).
Note the contribution policy from README (patches by email, PRs disabled) and the .openwikiignore-adjacent caveat that generated openwiki pages are not evidence.

State explicitly that the TLA+ specs, simulator drivers, workerd differential corpus, and live-fleet lab described in docs/testing.md are not present in this repository snapshot; engineers must not assume a local command runs them.

pages.title: HTTP listeners and the peer network
pages.purpose: HTTP surfaces: public ingress, internal listener, peer tunnel and HMAC auth, request URL policy, WebSocket ingress/egress, and forwarding/routing decisions.
instructions: Cover drain-time behavior: 503 new public requests, health transition, continued versioned peer traffic.
Document WebSocket ingress/egress and the outbound client; note the fastwebsockets unstable-split dependency rationale from Cargo.toml.
Document cell fetch/RPC dispatch: routing to the owner, tunneled plain HTTP inside signed establishment, replay/clock-window HMAC semantics, retry-after-failure predicates.
Document request identity handling: forwarded-header policy, host validation, request.url construction predicates, body limits and streaming threshold.

Document the two-listener policy: public Worker listener reserves only /.well-known/celld/health; internal listener serves peer protocol, operator routes, /peer/tunnel, /state, /reload, /shutdown, and 404s unknown paths.

pages.title: Node operations and memory pressure
pages.purpose: Operating nodes and fleets: configuration parsing, memory pressure and shedding, graceful shutdown and handoff, rolling updates, diagnose, and the operator API.
instructions: Document configuration parsing: env_vars.rs strictness (0/1 booleans, startup exit on invalid), CELLD_* table anchors in docs/README.md.
Document diagnose (lease enumeration + signed probe without taking a lease, restoring counter) and the operator API surface (/state, /reload, /shutdown[?handoff=preserve]).
Document memory pressure: threshold vs absolute cap math, cgroup working-set vs RSS, jemalloc slack, hysteresis release at 80%, shedding LRU idle cells, refusal to reacquire, /state inputs.
Document release engineering visible here: candidate-ref builds, attestations, container stages; note this is the only CI in the repo besides the openwiki workflow.

Document shutdown/rollout: health -> 503 path, batched handoff with L9 snapshot and L0 fallback, release/activation pacing knobs, drain token serialization, first-readiness fleet gate, node-log recovery takeover of a deadline-cut session.

pages.title: Telemetry and logging
pages.purpose: Observability: OTel traces and logs into the fleet bucket as Parquet, the OTLP sink, log capture/pipeline knobs, and node logging.
instructions: Distinguish this telemetry/node-log terminology carefully: the replicated node log is durability, not observability.

Document retention/flush knobs (CELLD_OTEL_RETENTION, flush time/bytes), sampler config, and the documented DuckDB query and compaction-job pattern; note celld does not compact its own telemetry files.
Document the sink contract: bucket default writes Parquet under telemetry/ partitioned by node and hour; otlp sink encodes protobuf by hand (otlp.rs).

Document what spans/logs are recorded (request spans, cell events, outbound fetch spans, cell-start spans, console.log records correlated with trace/span ids) and W3C traceparent propagation in and out.

pages.title: The celld-ltx replication engine
pages.purpose: The celld-ltx library: LTX capture from SQLite WAL, segment format and codec, compaction levels and bundles, replica clients, and restore mechanics.
instructions: Document ReplicaClient trait and backends (file, object_store), replica_url parsing, and error taxonomy.

Document levels and compaction: compaction_level definitions, streaming compactor, replica_compactor additive L1 behavior (destination created, source never deleted), bundle envelope as celld-original.
Document provenance: seeded from rustyriver/Litestream snapshot, leaser removal rationale, file-compatibility boundary with Litestream versions and CELLD_LTX_COMPACTION mixing rule.
Document the capture loop: WAL-mode setup, WAL->LTX segment capture, checkpoint takeover, durability position reporting.
Document the fault-injection oracle referenced by the Dockerfile test stage (sqlite3 CLI diffing) by locating it in tests.
Document the format stack: LTX v0.5.2 files, codec encode/decode, WAL parsing and SQLite cumulative checksums, reference/ltx-format.md.

pages.title: Reserved classes: D1, KV, Queues, cron, Workflows, assets
pages.purpose: The reserved-class platform services built on cells: D1, KV, Queues, cron, Workflows, static assets, and the operator CLIs that manage them.
instructions: Cover D1 (SQL execution, migrations, sqlite surface, d1_cli flow through a node to the owner), KV (namespace cells, value size/epoch handling from v0.4 notes, bulk Wrangler format), Queues (one reserved cell, admission 503 semantics, pause/resume), cron triggers (reserved cell + alarm arming via logic/cron), Workflows, and static assets (assets binding, _headers/_redirects, not-found handling).
Document the operator path: /runtime/<SCOPE> HMAC routes vs refused reserved classes on /do/<ID>.
Establish the pattern: each service is a reserved cell class (__-prefixed) with operator reachability through HMAC routes and celld CLI commands.
Keep the JS binding surface in runtime/v8-workers.md; this page covers the service-level state and control design.

pages.title: V8 runtime and the Workers JS layer
pages.purpose: How Worker code executes: rusty_v8 engine setup, JS bootstrap/harness, module loading, Durable Object bindings (storage, WebSocket, crypto, R2, fetch), and Wasm support.
instructions: Cover bindings: ctx.storage synchronous SQLite ops exposed to V8 with async JS wrapper, WebSocket hibernation surface, crypto, zlib, R2/KV/D1/Queue ops via reserved-class cells.
Cover heap limits: CELLD_V8_HEAP_LIMIT_MB default 128, 90% WebSocket admission, SQL materialization stop, 75% resume, forced collection on idle measurement.
Cover module loading and wasm compile-once-per-process reuse.
Document js.rs isolate turn execution and bootstrap.rs/harness.js layering; identify which behaviors are JS-side vs Rust ops.
Link to the V8 dependency note (rusty_v8 locker/Globals requirements) only as it appears in Cargo.toml comments.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical getting-started path for an engineer: build, run an example with celld dev, deploy to a bucket, run nodes, and find the right deep page per task.
instructions: Document: cargo build -p celld, the celld binary subcommands (dev, deploy, node, diagnose, cell, d1, kv, queue), running examples/hello and examples/counter with celld dev, and the Docker build path.
End with a short 'where to change what' routing map to the architecture, durability, runtime, deployment, operations, and change-guide pages.
State the minimum external prerequisites the repo establishes: esbuild on PATH for Worker deploys, a qualified bucket for fleet nodes, Linux/macOS targets from the release workflow.
Verify exact CLI surface from crates/celld/main.rs main() and crates/celld/main/cli.rs rather than assuming from README.
